VSS.title: vSet Select Operator's Guide Gen 3, 955703_2 (PDF, dealer-hosted)

CROP.title: vSet 2 Crop Setup Guide 955463_06 (PDF, PP Brandfolder)

qa.q: What has to be true before any control product (vDrive, DeltaForce etc.) will run?
qa.a: Typical requirements: system configured on the 20|20, its sensors/modules installed and configured, a default target (population or down force) set, an active speed source, the CCM Master Plant switch up, the implement reading lowered, and the system enabled on its control widget.
qa.tags: wont run not working requirements nothing happens

qa.q: Why does it say Master Off / the Master Plant safety warning keeps popping up?
qa.a: At every boot and after travelling more than half a mile, the 20|20 asks you to toggle the CCM Master Plant switch. If you press Cancel, no control system will operate until you toggle it, and a Master icon shows in the Status Center. Toggle Master Plant off and back up.
qa.tags: master off safety warning popup ccm switch

qa.q: I added the system but nothing shows on the home screen - what's missing?
qa.a: Each control system needs its Control widget on the home screen and enabled before it will function: press the Four Squares (top left) > Add Widget + > Controls, pick a size and place it.
qa.tags: widget home screen control button missing

qa.q: How do I set up the planter profile (make, rows, spacing)?
qa.a: Setup > Equipment > planter profile: choose Planter Make first (it defines later options), then Rows (choose Custom make if your row count isn't listed), Spacing ('Other' to type it), and Active Rows (All/Odd/Even/Left/Right/List). Effective Row Spacing and Effective Planter Width are calculated automatically and can be overridden if wrong.
qa.tags: planter make rows spacing profile equipment

qa.q: How do I add a system (seeding, down force, liquid, SmartFirmer) on newer software?
qa.a: On 2020.1.x and newer the equipment profile is organised by systems: press 'Add System' and configure each one (Seeding drive type and seed sensor type, Down Force system and sensor type, Liquid, Granular, Soil Sensing for SmartFirmer, Closing for FurrowForce). On current software, systems are added at Setup > Systems > Add Implement System, then hardware is added per system.

qa.q: Where do I set the row unit type and down force sensor type?
qa.a: Row unit type is in the Planter profile (Setup > Equipment > Planter); the Down Force Sensor Type options depend on the planter make/row unit chosen. On mixed row-unit planters use the Advanced screen to set row unit type per row and the correct load cell per row.
qa.tags: row unit type load cell sensor type mixed

qa.q: What GPS measurements do I need to enter for the planter?
qa.a: Setup > Equipment > Planter Measurements: choose Frame Type (Single, Dual Front for split-row, Dual Rear for pusher units, Center Trailing) and Hitch Style, then enter A Wheel Distance, B Seed Exit 1, and (frame-dependent) C Seed Exit 2, D and E off-centre distances. For a 3-point hitch measure to the tractor rear axle centre.
qa.tags: gps offsets planter measurements frame type hitch

qa.q: What tractor GPS measurements are needed?
qa.a: Setup > Equipment > Tractor Measurements: pick Steering type (Front, Track, Articulated) and enter the listed distances (hitch, centre-line offset, forward distance and height to the GPS output location). Some GPS systems don't output the antenna position - verify the output location with the GPS manufacturer.

qa.q: How do I run a GPS Offset Check?
qa.a: After entering planter and tractor measurements, choose GPS Offset Check in the Equipment menu. Needs good GPS and flat ground; works with front and track steering only. You set flags at the two outside gauge wheels, drive, turn around and stop with gauge wheels in the same spot facing the other way. Aim for 'Difference' near zero and use the Recommendations button.

qa.q: Should I save my tractor and planter configurations?
qa.a: Yes. Use Save/Load in the Equipment menu (Vehicles / Implements). Changing Implement Type resets configurations to factory defaults, so save before switching (e.g. planter to combine).
qa.tags: save load configuration implement type reset

qa.q: How do I set up lift switches?
qa.a: Setup > Systems > Lift Switch > Add Hardware. Push-button switches: choose rows and whether pushed-in means lifted or lowered (no calibration needed). Frame-mounted switch: plug location PDM, then Run Calibration and follow on-screen positions. Afterwards check 'Current State' changes correctly when you raise and lower.

qa.q: How do I calibrate the radar?
qa.a: Setup > Systems > Radar > Calibrate Radar. Needs good GPS and driving straight at least 300 ft at a constant 4 mph or more. If you already know Pulses Per Foot you can enter it manually. A tractor radar speed source is recommended for control products.
qa.tags: radar calibration speed source pulses per foot

qa.q: How do I set up the PDM and gyro?
qa.a: Setup > Systems > PDM: set Turn Rate Source ('Gyro Only' recommended), PDM Mounting Location (decal up/down) and Orientation (fuses forward/right/back/left), then 'Press to Zero' with the planter straight behind the tractor. Re-zero if turn compensation seems off. Compensation Setting 'On' is the recommended default.

qa.q: How do I change crop (e.g. maize to soybeans)?
qa.a: On current software Active Crop is chosen on the Field Setup screen (Setup > Fields > field > Crop). Seeds/disk, active rows, default population and population presets are Crop Settings saved per crop, so set them once with the new crop active. Remember the meter crop kit (disk/singulator/ejector) must be changed physically too.
qa.tags: change crop soybean corn maize crop settings

qa.q: What should Seeds to Average be?
qa.a: About 1% of population, e.g. 300 for 30,000 seeds/ac. It sets the rolling average for population, singulation and SRI.

qa.q: What do the CCM switches do?
qa.a: Left: Master Plant (must be up for any control product). Middle three: swath section switches (down = that section off). Raising the outside two middle switches together for one second auto-loads the meters; holding them keeps meters spinning. Right: Master Swath (down = all rows swathed off).
qa.tags: ccm cab control module switches autoload

qa.q: How does Quick Start work?
qa.a: Add the Quick Start widget; pressing it starts a countdown then meters spin at a simulated speed (3 mph per the Gen 3 planter guide) until real speed is detected or a timeout is reached (7 s in the older guide; the 2026 guide says up to 300 s and lets you set timeout and delay under Setup > Equipment > Speed Settings).

qa.q: How do I add vDrive hardware?
qa.a: Setup > Systems > [seeding system] > Hardware > Add Hardware > vDrive Primary: Step 1 select rows, Step 2 jumper colour (black is standard), Step 3 Auto-Assign rows, Step 4 set seeds/disk and swath output mode.

qa.q: What does the vDrive Manual Test check and when do I run it?
qa.a: Setup > Calibrations > [seeding system] > Manual Test, on every new install and at the start of each season. Watch for Actual vs Commanded RPM mismatch, >5% variation in duty cycle or motor stability between rows, >0.5 A variation in amps, or supply below 12 V. Seed is not required, but meters will drop seed if vacuum is on.

qa.q: What are normal vDrive diagnostic values?
qa.a: Motor stability typically 90-99%; current typically 0.4-0.9 A at 5 mph (depends on population and seeds/disk); supply voltage should be 12 V or more.

qa.q: vDrive shows yellow on Diagnose - why?
qa.a: Common causes: commanded RPM outside the drive's range; high amps (jamming, wrong disk shimming, motor damage); low voltage (harness damage or power overdraw - large SpeedTube/vDrive systems need double APEX power); low motor stability (damaged drive or rapidly changing rate zones).

qa.q: What do the vDrive LED blink patterns mean?
qa.a: No light = unpowered; solid = updating firmware; 1 Hz blink = healthy; 5 Hz blink = powered with an event code active; erratic blink = powered but no CAN communication.

qa.q: What vacuum should I run for maize (corn) with vSet 2?
qa.a: vSet 2 crop guide, field corn 1000-2800 seeds/lb: 20 inH2O with vSet/mSet, 20-25 inH2O with SpeedTube, 23 inH2O with vSet Select; baffle position 2; corn disk 730079 (27 holes, 0.176"), corn singulator 768355, corn ejector 768291. Treat these as starting points and check singulation.
qa.tags: vacuum corn maize inches water inh2o baffle disk

qa.q: Which disk for small maize seed?
qa.a: The crop guide notes that for corn above 2500 seeds/lb the 730085 Specialty disk (0.155" holes) often performs better than the 730079 corn disk - test both.

qa.q: What vacuum and parts for soybeans with vSet 2?
qa.a: Soybeans 2000-4500 seeds/lb: 20 inH2O vSet/mSet, 25-30 inH2O with SpeedTube, 24 inH2O vSet Select; baffle 2; kit 768342 (80-hole disk 730039) or the 56-hole kit 768690 (recommended with SpeedTube, under 140 seeds/s, and needs the soybean singulator).

qa.q: Small seeds leaking out of the bottom of the meter - what can I do?
qa.a: Crop guide: consider adding 1-2 small (0.010") disk shims, only as needed (they can raise vDrive current and reduce stability); remove them when converting back. Very small seeds (canola, sesame) should use the Small Seed Spacer 768811.

qa.q: Is eFlow / seed lubricant recommended?
qa.a: The vSet 2 crop guide recommends eFlow lubricant on all seeds at 1/8-1/4 cup per bag depending on seed size - do not over-apply.

qa.q: What are the WaveVision seed size limits?
qa.a: WaveVision needs the smallest seed dimension to be 0.150" or more; compatible crops are corn, soybeans, cotton, sugarbeets and edible beans (if they meet the size).

qa.q: How do I add vacuum sensors and zero them?
qa.a: Hardware > Add > Vacuum Sensor; assign rows to each sensor (unassigned rows won't build the vacuum map). To zero a false reading, read the sensor signal voltage at Setup > Diagnose > Planter > [seeding system] > Vacuum Sensor and enter it as the Offset (volts, not inH2O). vDrive does not require vacuum sensors.

qa.q: Population is wrong but meters seem fine - what to check first?
qa.a: Check Seeds/Disk matches the disk actually fitted (wrong seeds/disk gives wrong applied population), the active crop's settings, and that every row is assigned to a rate section (unassigned rows won't plant).
qa.tags: population wrong low high seeds per disk

qa.q: What does vSet Select need to run?
qa.a: vSet Select configured on the 20|20, a speed source, the CCM Master Plant switch up, and the planter lowered.

qa.q: How do I configure vSet Select?
qa.a: Setup > Equipment: confirm Planter Make, Rows, Spacing, Active Rows and Meter Type, set Drive Type to vSet Select and define the feed system. Then Setup > Systems > vSet Select: set Population Control (up to 4 rate sections - every row must be in one) and Swath Control (Disabled, Single Row, Dual Ends, Custom).
qa.tags: vset select setup feed system rate sections

qa.q: vSet Select starts or stops seeding at the wrong place - how do I fix it?
qa.a: First confirm GPS offsets and run a GPS Offset Check, and dig seeds to verify. Then use the vSet Select Calibration State: adjust Start Seeding Offset and Stop Seeding Offset independently, in inches (range -120 to 120). Increase the value to start/stop sooner, decrease to start/stop later. Measure the error by digging.
qa.tags: start stop offset early late headland calibration state clutch

qa.q: What calibrations must be done before vSet Select?
qa.a: Lift switches calibrated, radar calibrated (GPS and radar both recommended as speed sources), and PDM mounting location/orientation set with gyro zeroed. If already done for vDrive, no need to repeat.
qa.tags: calibration lift radar pdm vset select

qa.q: What is the Flow Reducer Offset?
qa.a: Only for the Mini Hopper feed system: each flow reducer has a sticker with a calibrated offset (its fully-open zero). That offset MUST be entered or the reducer won't fully open when needed.

qa.q: What does a multi-hybrid prescription need?
qa.a: At least two attributes - one for the orange meter and one for the blue meter. Only one prescription can be assigned per field; combine seeding/liquid/insecticide as separate attributes.
qa.tags: multi hybrid prescription attributes orange blue

qa.q: What does the default population / tank setting do?
qa.a: Default Population is used when no rate is commanded; you choose whether outside a prescription it uses Default or Current rate, and pick which tank (Orange or Blue) plants the default - i.e. a default rate and default hybrid.

qa.q: Should I use advanced swath tools (boundary recorder, simulated headlands) with WAAS?
qa.a: The guide says advanced swath tools should only be used with RTK-quality GPS; poorer GPS can give drifting boundaries and inaccurate clutch control.

qa.q: How do I set up SpeedTube on the 20|20?
qa.a: Equipment > Seeding > Seed Sensor Type = SpeedTube; then Systems > SpeedTube > Add Hardware > SpeedTube and select rows; set Active Rows and SpeedTube Auto-Unjam. Don't change the other settings unless your dealer says so. Check Diagnose is all green and run a health check (Manual Test under Seeding).

qa.q: When do SpeedTubes run and how do I stop them?
qa.a: They run whenever Master or any Section switch on the CCM is up, at minimum belt speed when the planter isn't moving. To stop them entirely, turn off Master and all three Section switches.

qa.q: Seeds dropping off the disk at higher speed with SpeedTube?
qa.a: Increase vacuum (via tractor hydraulics) - higher speeds/rougher ride can knock seeds off the disk before they reach the feeder wheels. For corn the crop guide starting range with SpeedTube is 20-25 inH2O.
qa.tags: speedtube vacuum high speed skips seeds drop

qa.q: What SpeedTube diagnostic values are expected?
qa.a: Help Center: drive amps above 0.5 A at 30 flights/s and above 4 A at 80; duty cycle above 30% at 30 flights/s and above 95% at 80; stability above 94% at 30 and above 96.5% at 80. Fix voltage problems first (check harness and alternator). Note: the page states supply volts 'should be less than 10' - this looks like an error in the source; confirm the expected voltage with your dealer.
qa.tags: speedtube diagnostics amps duty cycle stability volts

qa.q: Can I run Swath Run Cal with SpeedTube?
qa.a: No (older SeedSense quick reference): start with default Start/Stop Seeding Delay and Calibration Meter Speed, dig seeds once planting, and adjust delays manually after confirming GPS offsets.

qa.q: How do I switch SpeedTube from corn to soybeans?
qa.a: Snap the soybean deflector into the gearbox housing cavity (small feeder wheel stays); remove it to go back to corn. Meter crop kits must also be changed.

qa.q: SpeedTube annual / end-of-season maintenance?
qa.a: Remove belts in the off-season and reset tension before planting; check feeder wheels, housing, sensor lenses and pulleys; check opening disks and guards (replace guard with disks); remove SpeedTubes before power-washing (use compressed air or low-pressure water); check parallel-arm fasteners.

qa.q: How do I replace a SpeedTube belt?
qa.a: Remove sensor (hand knob), release lower cover tab and rotate cover off, roll belt off the bottom idler then top pulley. Fit new belt on top pulley, roll onto idler, check flight orientation against the moulded diagram, loosen the tension bracket screw, roll belt so the spring sets tension, retighten, refit cover until it clicks, refit sensor.

qa.q: What is singulation?
qa.a: The percentage of seeds properly singulated - the meter released one seed, not a skip or a multiple. The Skips/Multiples metric shows the breakdown of the rest.

qa.q: What is SRI and what value is bad?
qa.a: Seed Release Index measures spacing consistency of properly singulated seeds (skips/multiples excluded). Lower is better; 0 is perfect; above 32 is effectively random. SRI commonly becomes agronomically important at 20 or higher, so the SRI button turns yellow at 20 by default. Planter SRI will be higher than on a MeterMax stand.
qa.tags: sri seed release index spacing what is sri

qa.q: What does Good Ride mean?
qa.a: Percent of time row-unit ride quality is good enough not to hurt spacing. If SRI is high and Good Ride is high, slowing down may improve SRI.

qa.q: Is Average Spacing a measure of spacing accuracy?
qa.a: No - it's seeds divided by distance travelled, not an indication of spacing accuracy.

qa.q: How are skips and multiples shown on the map?
qa.a: On the Singulation map, singulated seeds are green, skips red and multiples blue.

qa.q: Lots of skips on one row - what should I check?
qa.a: Documented checks: vacuum level and whether that row's vacuum is reaching the meter (vacuum sensor/map), correct disk/singulator/ejector for the seed size, seeds/disk setting, vDrive diagnostics (high amps can mean jamming or wrong disk shimming), and at higher speeds with SpeedTube, more vacuum. A row-by-row mechanical diagnosis beyond these isn't in the public guides - ask your dealer.

qa.q: Lots of doubles/multiples - what should I check?
qa.a: The public guides don't give a doubles flowchart. Check the crop setup (disk/singulator/ejector/baffle and vacuum per the vSet 2 crop guide for your seed size) and dig to confirm. For anything further use the Dealer Service Manual troubleshooting via your dealer.

qa.q: What do the population limit and alarm settings do?
qa.a: Population Limit sets how far population can stray before it turns yellow; Population Alarm defines a Row Fail - the row's population dropping to that % of target (default 80%). Singulation, Ride Quality, Ground Contact and SRI limits set when those turn yellow.

qa.q: What DeltaForce target should I start with?
qa.a: DeltaForce starts in Standard (100 lb). Standard is a reasonable start on John Deere, Kinze or White planters at 5 mph (higher speeds may need more). On Case IH planters - and any planter with RID (reduced inner diameter) gauge wheels - Heavy (150 lb) is the recommended starter. First time out, err on the heavy side: shallow seed costs more than some compaction.
qa.tags: deltaforce target start standard heavy light 100 150

qa.q: What are the DeltaForce automatic modes?
qa.a: Light 50 lb, Standard 100 lb (default), Heavy 150 lb, Custom up to 195 lb - all targets for gauge-wheel load. Manual Mode applies one fixed lift and down force to all rows and ignores weigh pins.
qa.tags: light standard heavy custom 195 manual mode

qa.q: How do I know the downforce is set right?
qa.a: Aim for near 100% Ground Contact, use the down force map (blue dots = loss of contact), then dig: drive a few hundred feet with closing wheels up on a few rows; sidewalls should be formed and not crumble untouched, no slick/shiny compacted sidewall, seed in consistent moisture. 100% ground contact alone doesn't mean the setting is right.
qa.tags: how to set downforce dig furrow sidewall

qa.q: Should I change downforce after rain?
qa.a: The guide gives a big rain event as an example where a lighter setting may be needed to still form the right furrow - re-evaluate with the same tools (metrics, maps, digging).

qa.q: What do Margin and Ground Contact mean?
qa.a: Margin: the lowest load-cell reading per row over a period, averaged across load-cell rows. Ground Contact: % of time the gauge wheels are confirmed on the depth stop (load cell 20 lb or more).

qa.q: Which DeltaForce calibrations and when?
qa.a: Manual Test and Zero Load Sensors on every new install and every season start; New Install (Air Purge) on new installs and after replacing any hydraulic component. Zeroing is done fully raised and sensors should hold within +/-5 lb.
qa.tags: deltaforce calibration zero load sensors cells purge how to zero

qa.q: How do I do the DeltaForce Air Purge?
qa.a: Unpin and secure the bottom cylinder pins first (unpin rows either side if replacing one cylinder). Command 240 lb down for 10 s, back to 0; 180 lb lift for 10 s, back to 0; repeat until every cylinder has fully extended/retracted at least 3 times.

qa.q: How does the DeltaForce Manual Test work?
qa.a: Raise Lift Force Command to 450 lb (rows should lift), then with lift at 450 raise Down Force Command to 650 lb (rows should lower), then return both to 0. All rows lift together regardless of selection. Keep people clear.

qa.q: What hydraulic pressures should DeltaForce show?
qa.a: Hydraulics engaged: cylinder P-port and lift manifold PG-port 2250-3000 psi, R/L ports 0. During manual test at 650 down / 450 lift: P, L, PG, LG 2250-3000 psi; R and RG 0-100 psi.

qa.q: A load sensor failed mid-planting - what now?
qa.a: The system auto-ignores a suspect load sensor; an ignored row controls to the 80th percentile of the good rows. Override Force (static force, ignores sensors) is only a limp-home for multiple sensor failures. Don't change Maximum Down/Lift Force unless Product Support says so.
qa.tags: load sensor failed override limp home

qa.q: What is a healthy load cell reference value?
qa.a: Between 28 and 36 (varies across the planter but all should be in range). Zero load cells with the planter raised.

qa.q: What load cell calibration factor should each row unit use?
qa.a: From the Gen 3 guide: 1/2" load pin (JD 7000, Kinze 2000) 85; 5/8" load pin (JD XP and newer) 85; Kinze Link (Kinze 3000/4900) 65; White Smart Link (6000/8000) 65; White Smart Pin (9000/Precision Ready) 143; Case 1200 sensor 65; Case 2100 sensor 196; Monosem 5/8" pin (NG+ 3 and 4) 88. It auto-populates from make/sensor type.
qa.tags: calibration factor load pin kinze case white monosem

qa.q: DeltaForce shows yellow - common causes?
qa.a: Zero Load Sensors not done; wrong Sensor Type; or row unit selection incompatible with the load sensor. Red = damaged sensor/solenoid, disconnected or misconfigured; White = incomplete setup.

qa.q: What does AirForce need to run?
qa.a: Down Force system configured, down force sensors and Dual Pressure Modules installed and configured, default target set, speed source, CCM Master up, implement lowered, system enabled.

qa.q: How do I leak-test AirForce?
qa.a: Run Manual Test (Air Leak Check): command 100 lb lift then 100 lb down; actual psi should match command, supply should stay at or above 12 V, and the tank should hold with no command. To find a leak, command a target, press Done, then watch Diagnose > Airbag Down and Lift - dropping more than 2 psi/min suggests a leak.

qa.q: Can I change AirForce max pressures?
qa.a: Max Down Pressure and Max Lift Pressure should not be changed unless directed by Product Support. Tank Pressure Sensor is optional but encouraged for diagnostics.

qa.q: How do I set up SmartFirmer?
qa.a: SmartFirmers are configured in the Default (Implement) system: Setup > Systems > Default > Hardware > Add > SmartFirmer, select rows, Save and Finish. It needs the implement lowered to report.

qa.q: What are good SmartFirmer readings?
qa.a: Docs site: Uniform Furrow above 95%; Clean Furrow above 90% acceptable (95% goal in Panorama appendix); Soil Temperature above 10 C / 50 F; Furrow Moisture above 30% recommended for corn germination (note: the Panorama appendix says 'above 20%' - the two pages differ); Organic Matter usually 0.5-6%.
qa.tags: smartfirmer readings furrow moisture clean uniform temperature

qa.q: SmartFirmer shows dry furrow / low moisture - what do I do?
qa.a: Stop and dig to confirm; if dry, ensure planting depth reaches the moisture line. Causes can include cloddy conditions, sandy soil and knobs.

qa.q: One SmartFirmer reads differently from the others?
qa.a: Compare with neighbouring rows; inspect for soil build-up, damaged harness, condensation inside or scratched lens; also check the row unit mechanically (seized discs, plugged row cleaners, gauge wheel/disc shimming, worn discs).

qa.q: Can SmartFirmer control seeding rate?
qa.a: Yes - Sensor control on Seeding, Granular, Liquid and SmartDepth using OM or CEC ranges. Verify readings over several passes first. The first range needs max 100% and the last min 0%, each range's max equal to the previous range's min.
qa.tags: sensor control om cec variable rate

qa.q: Why doesn't the 20|20 show SmartFirmer maps?
qa.a: The 20|20 does not display SmartFirmer maps; Panorama shows them.

qa.q: Can I silence the SmartFirmer soil temp alarm?
qa.a: Alerts and alarms can't be disabled separately; set the alarm value to something unreachable (e.g. Soil Temperature Alarm 1 F).

qa.q: How do I make CleanSweep row cleaners more or less aggressive?
qa.a: Cab controller lever RIGHT = pressure in DOWN (more aggressive); LEFT = pressure in LIFT (less aggressive). Don't use row cleaners to move soil - it causes uneven depth.

qa.q: What air does CleanSweep need?
qa.a: 120+ psi of clean, dry air from the CleanSweep or AirForce compressor. OEM compressors aren't supported and can void cylinder warranty. With an AirForce compressor, it won't build pressure until AirForce is enabled on the 20|20.

qa.q: CleanSweep compressor won't turn on?
qa.a: Check the power harness fuse; check 12 V on pins 1 and 2 of the 3-pin round connector (pin 3 ground); then jumper the pressure switch 2-pin connector - if it runs, replace pressure switch 755054, if not, replace relay 755095.
qa.tags: compressor wont turn on fuse relay

qa.q: CleanSweep compressor runs too often or never stops?
qa.a: Runs too often: leaks - do the leak test. Never shuts off at 150+ psi: replace pressure switch 755054.

qa.q: CleanSweep maintenance?
qa.a: Daily: drain the water separator and check for leaks. Every 100 h: drain the tank, clean the air filter pre-cleaner. Yearly: replace pre-cleaner and filter (726546) and leak test. Plug/cap air lines when unhooking.

qa.q: How do I rate-check FurrowJet?
qa.a: GPM per row = GPA x MPH x row spacing (in) / 5940. E.g. 10 GPA, 5 mph, 30" = 0.2525 GPM per row (ounces/min = GPM x 128). Catch output under the nozzles at planting pump RPM/pressure; with water apply the fertiliser conversion factor. Target at least 30 psi at the orifice.

qa.q: FurrowJet nozzle plugged?
qa.a: External: use the brush; avoid running wings too high. Internal: clean strainer (maybe finer, plus in-line strainers), blow out with air can, remove and clean nozzle with the tool; frequent plugging may need the updated manifold/splitter.

qa.q: FurrowJet maintenance and storage?
qa.a: Keep nozzles/manifolds clean, plug open lines when removed, replace wing at the wear mark, keep openers at least 14.5" and correctly shimmed, flush periodically and at year end, never reverse in the ground, park the planter raised.

qa.q: How do I set up Conceal?
qa.a: Conceal isn't covered in the docs gathered for this demo - please ask your dealer (PSS Ag) or see the current docs site guides.

qa.q: How do I load a seeding prescription?
qa.a: Shapefiles (.shp, .shx, .dbf) on the USB root or in a 'Sendto2020' folder: Setup > Data > Import > Prescription/Boundary. Or activate a Panorama plan (Setup > Fields > Active Field > Planning). Then assign the prescription and attribute to each rate section on the field's Prescriptions tab.

qa.q: Prescription loaded but planting a flat rate?
qa.a: An attribute must be assigned to each rate section, and Control Mode must be set to Prescription (vSet Select: Variable). A yellow indicator means a prescription is assigned but a manual rate is being planted.

qa.q: What happens outside the prescription?
qa.a: It plants the Default Population (vSet Select lets you choose Default or Current rate when leaving the prescription).

qa.q: What are rate sections?
qa.a: Single = one rate across all rows; Multiple = up to 4 different targets across preconfigured sections, set in System Settings > Control Sections.

qa.q: How do swath offsets and coverage patterns work?
qa.a: Row Offset (none, 1/2 row, 1 row, custom) sets the start/stop distance from headlands; for multi-row sections choose Underplant, 50-50 or Overplant.

qa.q: What do the Diagnose colours mean?
qa.a: Green OK; Yellow not 100%; Red failed or expected but not detected; White detected but not expected; Black disabled; Grey detecting/unreachable; Teal updating firmware (current docs). All should be green before going to the field.
qa.tags: diagnose colours green yellow red white

qa.q: Everything after one module is red - why?
qa.a: On 2023.1.0+ software, after Reset Modules or a power cycle, a daisy-chain break in the harness makes every component after it show red. Fix the harness break first.

qa.q: What does Reset Modules do?
qa.a: It breaks and re-establishes CAN communication and daisy-chain identification - a standard first step for communication problems.

qa.q: Where do I see error/event codes?
qa.a: Setup > Diagnose > Event Log: newest first, each with number, time and description; tap for details; filter by system.

qa.q: Support asked for a detailed log - how?
qa.a: Diagnose > Advanced Logs > Enable Detailed Log (runs 1 minute), then Export - System Data Log to USB. Or Data > Export > Support Data uploads logs (needs WiFi).

qa.q: What's the difference between alert and alarm sounds?
qa.a: Alert plays when an item is yellow on the home screen; Alarm when it's red. Set in Systems > Display > Sound.

qa.q: What does Row Fail Action do?
qa.a: Sets what the screen does on a row failure: Jump to Row (row details), Jump to Dashboard, or None.

qa.q: What health checks are available?
qa.a: Diagnose > Health Checks runs product-specific checks that give a report card; always run after install or long storage.

qa.q: Display reads wrong voltage / low voltage issues?
qa.a: Many modules want 12 V or more (vDrive, SmartFirmer, AirForce DPM). Low voltage points to damaged power/CAN harnessing or overdraw; big SpeedTube/vDrive systems need double APEX power.

qa.q: What does 'Reset Settings' vs 'Factory Reset' do?
qa.a: Reset Settings returns ALL display, tractor, planter and control-product configs to default. Factory Reset wipes all data from the Display Base Module. Back up first.

qa.q: How do I export field data to USB?
qa.a: Setup > Data > Export (USB in the left side of the display): Field Map Data (Transfer All or Selected Fields), Field & Crop Config, Prescription/Boundary, Swath Coverage Map, Equipment Config, Display Config.

qa.q: How does data get to Panorama?
qa.a: Pair a Gen 3 20|20 (2024.1 software or newer) with Panorama; with stable WiFi/internet it uploads the active field as you go. For inactive fields and upload progress, use the Export page in 20|20 settings. Gen 2 / other displays need manual upload.

qa.q: How do I get Panorama data into FieldView?
qa.a: In Panorama: Log In > Manage Operation > Data Sharing > toggle FieldView on > Continue > log into FieldView > Allow.

qa.q: How do I back up the whole monitor?
qa.a: Data > Backup/Restore > Backup All to a USB on the DBM (internal memory is 32 GB, so use a large enough drive). Check Backup Status compares the USB with the monitor. Restore All duplicates; Restore Config brings back configs only.

qa.q: Can I share coverage between two planters in the same field?
qa.a: Export the Swath Coverage Map from one display and import it into the other; or with FieldView modules, enable Shared Swath on all 20|20s.

qa.q: How do I update the 20|20 software?
qa.a: Data > Software Update. Install from USB: download free from Precision Planting (2020.ag / support site), put the file on the USB root, insert in the display, choose the version and wait for the reboot (updates DBM and display; a second display may need another reboot/update). Or Install over WiFi.

qa.q: Modules show teal / grey after an update?
qa.a: Teal = updating firmware; grey = detecting/unreachable. Let them finish; if they stay grey, Reset Modules and check harnessing.

qa.q: Which guide version should I follow?
qa.a: Docs-site guides are written for specific software (e.g. 2025.1.x or 2026.0.0); older guides are on cloud.precisionplanting.com. Check Systems > Display > About for your version.

qa.q: What should I do with the 20|20 at season end?
qa.a: Back up everything (Data > Backup All to USB) and export field data. Then update software before next season if needed.

qa.q: How should I store vSet meters over winter?
qa.a: An official Precision Planting vSet storage procedure wasn't found in the public docs gathered. Ask your dealer. The documented related items: remove SpeedTube belts off-season, flush liquid systems at year-end, drain CleanSweep air system.

qa.q: Start-of-season checklist?
qa.a: Documented items: vDrive Manual Test; DeltaForce/AirForce Manual Test and Zero Load Sensors; SpeedTube health check and belt tension; lift switch/radar/GPS offset check if anything changed; confirm crop settings (seeds/disk, vacuum per crop guide).

qa.q: How much hydraulic pressure does DeltaForce need from the tractor?
qa.a: DeltaForce Gen 3 guide, Hydraulic Pressure Requirements: Supply Pressure greater than 2250 psi, Return Pressure less than 100 psi, and Lift Pressure between 200 psi and the supply pressure. Low hydraulic pressure limits DeltaForce performance (the Low Pressure popup warns you unless it has been disabled in Advanced Setup). The guide doesn't give a tractor flow (gpm) figure - check flow/SCV setup with your dealer.
